I'm sizing effort for a Jira enhancement ticket (SFCC-724, "SEO – Indexable Filter Pages with Per-Filter Metadata") in the Zimmermann PWA Kit repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. This is read-only research to inform a story-point/days estimate — do not edit anything.

Ticket description verbatim: "As a Site Merchandiser, I want to flag specific filter combinations (e.g. Dresses + White) as indexable pages with their own clean URL and metadata, so that Zimmermann can rank for high-value search terms like 'white dresses' without having to create and maintain a separate category for each one. Currently, all filtered PLP URLs canonicalise back to the base category page per DMU-023, meaning Google does not index them as standalone pages. This enhancement would allow a merchandiser to opt specific filter combinations into indexability via Business Manager, and set a unique title tag, meta description, and SEO paragraph per combination. The PWA Kit would then render the correct metadata for those URLs."

I need answers to these, with file:line citations:

1. **Current canonical/SEO behavior for PLP filter URLs.** Read `overrides/app/components/seo/` (whatever exists there) — what does it currently render (title, meta description, canonical tag), and where does the canonical-back-to-base-category behavior (referenced as "DMU-023") actually live in code? Is it in the Seo component, the PLP page container, or a routing/URL-building layer?

2. **PLP filter URL structure today.** Are filters currently represented as query params only, or does any clean/pretty-URL-per-filter-combination routing already exist anywhere (check `overrides/app/routes.tsx` and any PLP-related routing/URL-building code, e.g. use-navigation hook usage)? I need to know whether "clean URL per filter combo" is greenfield routing work or something partially there already.

3. **Any existing SFCC-side or Contentful-side pattern for per-URL/per-entity custom metadata** (title tag / meta description / a body paragraph) that this could reuse — e.g. does Contentful already model an SEO content type, or does any existing PDP/PLP/CMS page already fetch custom title+description+body text keyed by a slug/identifier? Check `.docs/prd/plp.md`, any `.docs/integration/*seo*` or `*contentful*` doc, and `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` / content-type definitions under `scripts/contentful/content-types/`.

4. **Search `.docs/` for "DMU-023"** (the label/decision ID this ticket cites) and quote what you find — I need to know if this canonicalization rule is documented anywhere with more context than the ticket gives.

5. **Any existing SEO integration doc** — check `.docs/integration/` for a numbered SEO doc (e.g. `NN-seo.md`) and summarize anything relevant to metadata rendering, canonical tags, or PLP indexability if one exists.

Report back concisely (under 400 words) with direct file:line references for every claim. I mainly need: how much of this is genuinely new build vs. reusing existing plumbing, and whether the "clean URL" part implies new routing work. Don't speculate beyond what the code/docs actually show — say plainly if something doesn't exist.

Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. 1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
58	        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
59	        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
60	        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
61	        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
62	        │
63	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
64	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
65	        │
66	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
67	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
68	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
69	```
70	
71	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
72	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
73	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
74	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
79	|---|---|---|
80	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
81	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
82	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
83	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
84	
85	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
86	
87	## 5. Data exchanged
88	
89	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
92	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
93	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
94	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
95	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
96	
97	No PII flows through Contentful.
98	
99	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
100	
101	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
102	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
103	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
104	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
105	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
106	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
107	
108	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
109	
110	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
111	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
112	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
113	
114	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
115	
116	| Failure | Behaviour |
117	|---|---|
118	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
119	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
120	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
121	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
122	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
123	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
124	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
125	
126	## 9. Security and privacy
127	
128	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
129	- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages, both of which return 404 when no token is present. Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
130	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
131	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
132	
133	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
134	
135	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
136	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
137	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

18	const fallback = <Skeleton height="75vh" width="100%" />;
19	// Base routes deliberately not served. `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` reads this list so the

21	const EXCLUDED_BASE_ROUTES = ['/category/:categoryId'];

23	// Create your pages here and add them to the routes array
24	// Use loadable to split code into smaller js chunks
25	const Home = loadable(() => import('./pages/home'), { fallback });
26	const MyNewRoute = loadable(() => import('./pages/my-new-route'));
27	const ContentfulPreview = loadable(() => import('./pages/contentfulPreview'), { fallback });
28	const CheckoutError = loadable(() => import('./pages/checkout-error'), { fallback });
29	const CheckoutRedirect = loadable(() => import('./pages/checkout-redirect'), { fallback });
30	/*
31	 * Same trap as ProductDetail/ProductList: the base app/routes.jsx loads the confirmation page
32	 * with a relative import that the overrides resolver never redirects. Without this explicit
33	 * entry the Adyen confirmation override is dead code and the base page renders instead.
34	 */
35	const CheckoutConfirmation = loadable(() => import('./pages/confirmation'), { fallback });
36	
37	/*
38	 * The PDP override is reached through this explicit entry, not through the overrides
39	 * resolver. That resolver only redirects imports that *name* `@salesforce/retail-react-app`;
40	 * the base `app/routes.jsx` loads its PDP with a relative `import('./pages/product-detail')`,
41	 * which is never redirected. Without the route below, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail`
42	 * is dead code and the base page renders instead.
43	 */
44	const ProductDetail = loadable(() => import('./pages/product-detail'), { fallback });
45	
46	// Same trap as ProductDetail above: the base app/routes.jsx loads PLP with a relative
47	// `import('./pages/product-list')`, which the overrides resolver never redirects. Without the
48	// two routes below, `overrides/app/pages/product-list` is dead code and the base page renders
49	// instead. Base routes.jsx uses this same component for both '/search' and
50	// '/category/:categoryId' — mirrored here as two entries pointing at the one override.
51	const ProductList = loadable(() => import('./pages/product-list'), { fallback });
52	
53	// Hierarchical category URLs (/clothing/dresses/day-dresses, SEO PRD DMU-014): the dispatcher
54	// resolves any unmatched path to a category (PLP), a single-segment Contentful experience page, or
55	// not-found. The base '/category/:categoryId' shape is not served at all — see `..._routes` below.
56	const CategoryPath = loadable(() => import('./pages/categoryPath'), { fallback });
57	
58	// SFCC-84 Recently Viewed Full History page (build plan §B2) — a genuinely new route, not an
59	// override of any base page, so there is no relative-vs-package-path trap like ProductDetail/
60	// ProductList above.
61	const RecentlyViewed = loadable(() => import('./pages/recentlyViewed'), { fallback });
62	
63	const routes = [
64	  {
65	    path: '/',
66	    component: Home,
67	    exact: true,
68	  },
69	  {
70	    path: '/my-new-route',
71	    component: MyNewRoute,
72	  },
73	  // Must precede `..._routes` — the base array carries its own '/product/:productId'
74	  // entry pointing at the base page, and `configureRoutes` keeps the first match.

78	  },
79	  // Same reasoning as ProductDetail above — the base array carries its own '/search' entry

86	  { path: '/checkout/error', component: CheckoutError, exact: true },

88	  // The base '/category/:categoryId' route is dropped rather than shadowed: category pages live

90	  ..._routes.filter((route: { path?: string }) => !EXCLUDED_BASE_ROUTES.includes(route.path ?? '')),
91	  // Contentful Live Preview — must be before /:slug so it takes priority.
92	  {
93	    path: '/preview',
94	    component: ContentfulPreview,
95	    exact: true,
96	  },
97	  // No ordering constraint versus `..._routes` above — the base array has no '/recently-viewed'

106	  // other route matched. CategoryPath renders the Experience page itself for a single-segment path
107	  // that is not a category.
108	  {
109	    path: '/:segments+',
110	    component: CategoryPath,
111	  },

117	    ignoredRoutes: ['/callback', '*'],

1	# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
10	- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
11	- Basket and cart
12	- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
13	- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
14	- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
15	- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission
16	
17	At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).
18	
19	Out of scope of this document:
20	
21	- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
23	- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
24	- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages
25	
26	## 2. Browser-side architecture
27	
28	```
29	PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
30	        │
31	        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
32	        ▼
33	SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
34	        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
35	        ▼
36	SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	SFCC realm
40	```
41	
42	- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
43	- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
44	- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.
45	
46	## 3. Authentication and credentials
47	
48	- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
49	- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
50	- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
51	- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
52	- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.
53	
54	### Magento password migration (CFD-013)
55	
56	Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.
57	
58	### Cross-storefront session continuity
59	
60	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.
61	
62	- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
63	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
64	- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
65	- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.
66	
67	## 4. Data exchanged
68	
69	| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
70	| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
72	| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
73	| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
74	| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
75	| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
76	| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
77	| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
78	| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |
79	
80	Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.
81	
82	## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)
83	
84	- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
85	- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86	- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
87	- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
88	
89	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
90	
91	- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
92	- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
93	- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
94	- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
95	- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
96	- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.
97	
98	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
99	
100	SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):
101	
102	| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
103	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
